about.background: I am a student at the School of Information Science and Engineering, University of Jinan, and a member of the MLNBA Lab. My research interests focus on network security measurement, intelligent threat detection, and trustworthy security analysis. My current research explores encrypted traffic analysis, IPv6 network measurement, asset discovery, and AI-driven security analytics, with the goal of developing practical and interpretable methods for understanding and defending complex cyberspace environments.
about.interests:
My research interests focus on network security measurement, intelligent threat detection, and trustworthy security analysis. I am interested in leveraging machine learning, knowledge graphs, large language models, and security analytics techniques to analyze network traffic, security logs, threat intelligence, vulnerability information, and software artifacts for attack detection, attack-chain correlation, threat tracing, and risk assessment. In particular, I hope to study encrypted traffic metadata analysis, IPv6 network measurement and asset discovery, multi-source security intelligence fusion, threat intelligence knowledge graphs, software supply chain security, and LLM-assisted vulnerability analysis. 
Beyond network security analytics, I am also interested in exploring the integration of cryptographic techniques, privacy-preserving computation, and digital content security with intelligent security analysis, including privacy-aware threat detection, secure collaborative analysis, and the identification of malicious or manipulated information in complex cyberspace environments. My long-term goal is to develop automated, interpretable, privacy-aware, and generalizable security analysis methods that can be effectively deployed for real-world attack detection, attribution, and defense.

projects.name: Distribute Zmap
projects.highlights: Distribute Zmap delivers a scalable distributed scanning framework with robust task orchestration and significantly enhanced IPv6 stability and crash resilience compared to the official Zmap project.
projects.description: Distribute Zmap is an enhanced and scalable version of the official Zmap project, specifically engineered for large-scale distributed scanning and improved IPv6 functionality.

projects.name: Sentinel Gateway
projects.highlights: A proprietary multi-evidence fusion engine for application identification — leveraging weighted scoring across 9 evidence categories instead of traditional port matching. Features real-time Zero Trust and DLP integration for risk-adaptive policy enforcement, AI-assisted asynchronous policy generation and event analysis without compromising 10 Gbps wire-speed throughput, and full OpenAppFilter ecosystem compatibility with an independently developed, fully controllable full-stack architecture.
projects.description: Designed for 10Gbps high-speed networks, Sentinel Gateway is an intelligent Internet behavior security management system. By converging multi-evidence application identification, Zero Trust dynamic risk assessment, DLP, and an AI Security Copilot into a unified gateway, it achieves a comprehensive, closed-loop security governance cycle: Identify, Assess, Protect, and Audit.

projects.name: SecureLink
projects.highlights: SecureLink’s highlights are a strong Go-based backend, a modern Vue + TypeScript frontend, and a full-stack architecture that balances performance, usability, and maintainability.
projects.description: A lightweight, security-focused link management project designed to protect and share URLs safely with simple, reliable access control.

projects.name: MAT: Security Monitoring and Profiling for AI Agent Ecosystems
projects.highlights: Builds evidence-backed agent inventories, capability profiles, and dependency graphs from multiple external signals.  Maintains provenance-aware, versioned profiles to track role drift, node failures, and topology changes.   Uses adaptive probing and uncertainty-aware reasoning to reduce false identification under incomplete or conflicting evidence.
projects.description: MAT provides external security visibility for partially observable AI agent ecosystems. It discovers agents from authorized, unlabeled endpoints and combines protocol probing, behavioral validation, evidence fusion, and LLM reasoning to identify, roles, capabilities, dependencies, and ecosystem changes without application or host-side instrumentation.
